prep.note: You cannot pre-write. Build a story bank of 3–4 challenge stories and 3–4 team stories, beats only, not scripts. Rehearse the reflection, not the story. Practise writing and submitting 335 words in 10 minutes. Run the Kira practice module repeatedly; it's unlimited and unscored.

postSystem.body: Life Sciences is an admission category, not a program of study. In first year you are not enrolled in any specific program. You apply to your subject POSt at the end of first year, on your first-year university marks.

types.name: Open programs
types.requirement: No requirements beyond completing 4.0 credits. Enrol directly on ACORN.

types.name: Limited programs
types.requirement: Specific courses, minimum grades, sometimes a supplementary application or essay. High-demand ones use a variable minimum grade, the cutoff is re-set every year from that year's applicant pool. There is no published number to aim at in advance.

postSystem.mechanics: Two request periods per year. You must enrol in a valid program combination in the session you pass 4.0 credits.

traps.title: You are not applying to a program
traps.body: Getting into Life Sci is not getting into the program you want. That decision is a year away and runs on your first-year university marks, against a cutoff that doesn't exist until it's set.

traps.title: The prerequisites are lighter than everyone assumes
traps.body: Admission requires English and Grade 12 Calculus only. No Biology, no Chemistry. But U of T's own example: for psychology you need ENG4U and calculus to be admitted, and Grade 12 biology to enrol in the psychology program at the end of first year. You can be admitted and then find you can't take the courses your intended POSt requires.

traps.title: St. George and UTM have opposite prerequisite shapes
traps.body: St. George requires MCV4U and only recommends the sciences. UTM requires MHF4U plus SBI4U plus SCH4U and only recommends MCV4U. Separate OUAC codes, separate decisions. This is the one people get wrong.

traps.title: You can switch out of your category later
traps.body: You may apply to programs outside your admission category at the end of first year. Life Sci is not a cage; it's the door you came in through.

rules: You may apply to up to three programs or campuses, but only one application per program area. You cannot apply to two program areas within A&S St. George.

adjustmentFactor.body: Waterloo applies an adjustment factor based on how students from your high school have historically performed at Waterloo. It compares their first-year university averages against their final high school averages, over the past six or more years. Your admission average is not your admission average.

aiScoring.body: Waterloo states the AIF is reviewed both by trained human reviewers and by artificial intelligence. If the scores differ significantly, a second human scorer reviews the submission. aiScoring.contrast: Waterloo discloses using AI to score the AIF while explicitly prohibiting applicants from using AI to write it. Waterloo reserves the right to revoke an offer if it believes the AIF was not self-written.
aiScoring.note: None of Rotman, Queen's or McMaster disclose AI involvement in scoring anywhere in their public FAQs.

alternativeOffer.body: If you select the Rotman Commerce or Computer Science admission categories, you can select a second A&S admission category for consideration on the Join U of T portal. It does not affect eligibility for your first choice, and is evaluated after all first-choice applicants have been considered.
alternativeOffer.note: Rotman is the only program in this set with a real built-in fallback. Queen's makes no alternate offers. Western makes no automatic alternatives. Always set a second category: Social Sciences is the natural one. It costs nothing.

traps.title: Rotman's own pages disagree about the December deadline
traps.body: The Important Dates page says submitting after 1 December means they may not consider you until after the March round, then adds an asterisk saying all Ontario secondary school applicants are treated equally so long as documents arrive by the regular deadline. The Ontario High School Applicants page says late submission means April or May. Best reading for an Ontario student: the asterisk applies to you. But it's not stated cleanly anywhere. Hit 1 December: nothing is lost by being early.

traps.title: Grade 11 counts
traps.body: Rotman states all Grade 11 and 12 U/M courses may be considered, and recommends an overall average of all Grade 11 and 12 courses in the mid-high 80s or above. No other program in this set says this.

traps.title: Night school and private credits are discouraged in writing
traps.body: Rotman reserves the right to give preference to students whose marks are the result of a single attempt at each course, and encourages students to take courses in their day school where possible.

traps.title: Rotman and Queen's Commerce are different programs
traps.body: Similar names, different schools, different OUAC codes, different deadlines, different supp app formats. Rotman also uses the general Join U of T portal while U of T Engineering applicants use a separate one.

prep.note: The activities list and the intro video should be finished, timed and polished weeks in advance. 20 minutes for a 200-word written answer is real drafting time, unlike Queen's 10 minutes for 335 words. Practice sessions are unlimited: use them until the intro video is clean. Specificity about Rotman itself (streams, specializations, resources) is reported to matter in the intro video.

programs.howToApply: OUAC → University of Toronto → Faculty of Arts & Science, St. George → then select Rotman Commerce from the program list. It is an A&S admission category, not a separate faculty application. After applying you get a U of T confirmation email with your JOINid/UTORid. Documents may take up to three weeks to appear on Join U of T. Safe-list utoronto.ca.
